comment: Tier 0 only. Magpie drives real benchmarks and kernel builds on GPU
hardware, so no case grades behavior yet; add one with `should` /
`should_not` plus an evals/machine.yml when a runner is available.
The boundary that matters here is against tracelens-analysis-orchestrator:
both mention TraceLens and trace analysis, so 'benchmark and optimize
kernels' versus 'orchestrate a trace analysis report' is the thing most
likely to route wrong. `benchmark-then-optimize-kernel` is that line, in the
words someone would use when they mean this skill.

expected_matches.prompt: Benchmark vLLM throughput and time-to-first-token for Llama 3 on this box, and capture torch traces while it runs.
I have two HIP implementations of a softmax kernel. Which one is faster, and is the optimized one still numerically correct?
Find the top bottleneck kernels in my inference workload and map the profiler names back to the source that generates them.
Rank these three Triton attention kernel variants against each other and validate the winner end to end.

expected_matches.note: Trace-analysis vocabulary shared with tracelens-analysis-orchestrator, but the work is benchmarking and kernel ranking.
expected_matches.prompt: Benchmark SGLang on this node, then rank two candidate HIP kernels for the biggest bottleneck and validate the winner.

expected_no_matches.note: Kernel authoring, not kernel evaluation. Shares all the vocabulary and none of the workflow.
expected_no_matches.prompt: Write a CUDA kernel that transposes a matrix, and explain the shared-memory tiling.

expected_no_matches.note: A datasheet question, not a measurement to run.
expected_no_matches.prompt: What is the theoretical peak FP16 throughput of an MI300X on paper?
